Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X71/X71n1420.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Chushi Fanqi (楚石梵琦禪師語錄): Chushi Fanqi says bogus Chan fellows are as numerous as hemp and grain while criticizing two inherited interpretations.

Senses.Explanation: A fabricated Chan fellow is a recurring rebuke for someone who invents confident encounter-talk without having read the situation. Dahui Zonggao contrasts true connoisseurs with contemporary bogus fellows who would mistake the cited speaker’s silence for having been defeated. Yuansou Xingduan dismisses a newcomer with the phrase after an inadequate reply and says such fellows are as plentiful as hemp and grain. A transmission biography records Zhan’tang Wenzhun giving the same rebuke when the visiting monk answers his challenge about a missing half of the nose. The insult targets counterfeit encounter competence, not literary authorship.
